newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds edge up on lack of supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds edge up on lack of supply.

text.p: Light buying amid a shortage of supply bolstered the prices of U.S. fixed-rate pass-through securities on Thursday, traders said.
Additionally, they said some secondary market players got a chance to sink their teeth into a $616 million Adjustable Rate Mortgage (ARM) bid list, released earlier in the afternoon.
"Several people have sold the list and the market has been focused on that," one trader in New York said.
Nevertheless, buyers of fixed-rate mortgages kept yield spreads to Treasuries slightly tighter since there was a lack of supply from mortgage bankers, traders said.
"(Spreads) have tightened rather dramatically the last couple of days and they were...a little tighter today," one trader said.

Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were up 1/32 at 100-25/32 bid, yielding 118 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 1/32 higher as well, at 100-24/32 bid and 100-30/32 bid, respectively.
The five-year Treasury note was unchanged at 99-20/32 bid to yield 6.71 percent, while the 10-year Treasury note was 2/32 higher to yield 6.86 percent.
Mortgage sources said many traders were sidelined until Friday's March jobs data, waiting to see if Treasuries break out of their trading range.

"If people get comfortable that we are in a trading range, I think spreads will be fine," the source said. "If people get the feeling that the (Federal Reserve) is going to have to tighten again, sooner rather than later, I think that will put pressure on (mortgages)."
